application_guidance.input_pattern: Exact value-gradient access with global gradient and Hessian Lipschitz bounds and dimension-uniform epsilon-stationarity objective.

complexity_scope.guarantee: Per-fixed-instance probability >=2/3; least almost-sure query cap, not expected query complexity.
complexity_scope.hidden_constants: Absolute numerical constants; dimension is not optimized.
complexity_scope.oracle: Exact function-value and gradient bundle at an arbitrary Euclidean point.
complexity_scope.output_and_metric: Any x_hat in R^d, queried or unqueried; ||gradient f(x_hat)||<=epsilon.
complexity_scope.resource: Number of exact first-order oracle calls; supremum of the dimension-specific complexities over all finite d.
complexity_scope.upper_witness_or_lower_coverage: All measurable adaptive randomized algorithms described above; no linear-span or zero-respecting restriction.

content.intended_use: Supply the literature randomized lower bound, with its precise model and parameter window.

proofs.locator: Sections 4–8, pp.5–16; equations (8)–(10), (22), (28)–(32); Proposition 8.1 and proof of Theorem 3.1
map: Calibration: h=H epsilon, gamma=c_gamma sqrt(L2 h), R=h/gamma, D=h²/gamma, M=floor(c_M sqrt(L1/gamma)), N=floor(c_N Delta/D), m=floor(M/2), T0=4NM. Regime constants ensure M,N>=2 and NM has the claimed parameter dependence.

Import Lemmas 5.1–5.4: smooth flat gate/saturation/radial squash, finite spectral dual residual and moment/short-Krylov estimates. Construction 5.1 keeps positive quadratic matrices permanently present and gates only bounded positive forcing.

Proposition 6.1 proves every realization belongs to the target class: local Hessian scale O(gamma), third derivative O(gamma²/h), bounded local overlap and initial gap O(ND). Lemma 6.3 uses two gradient projections, linear saturation and positive forcing to require all first N-1 gates open and final residual <=epsilon at every epsilon-stationary point.

Definition 7.1 reveals (u_s,b_s) at tau_s=1+(s-1)m and U_s only at sigma_s=1+sm. Lemma 7.1 conditions on other blocks' raw independent draws, not adaptive transcripts; before retirement, queries lie in Gaussian-start Krylov spans plus degree <=t-tau_s RHS span.

Lemma 7.2 chooses sufficiently large spectral multiplicities independently of policy. Its projection bound and radial direction preservation yield |v_s|<=1/4 before retirement. Lemma 7.3 couples censored and true value-gradient transcripts by induction, since omitted gates and their derivatives vanish.
Lemma 7.4 excludes stationary queries before 1+Nm: before final activation an earlier gate is flat; afterward the final residual condition forces v_N>=3/4, contradicting its active-block barrier.

Proposition 8.1 fixes the distribution independently of policy, with simultaneous good-event probability at least 5/6. An unqueried terminal output is appended as one final query, changing constants. Fixing each private seed and averaging gives the randomized lower bound by the distributional direction of Yao's principle.
proofs.omitted_details: Source-linked long literature proof, not a new local lemma or transfer. Appendix primitive/spectral-design proofs and cited external interfaces are imported, not independently reproved. The Li–Lin predecessor paper was not independently read.
proofs.reading_coverage: Direct original-PDF extraction pp.4–16 read; attached pp.1–10 visually inspected. Statement, calibration, construction interfaces, membership/stationarity and Sections 7–8 arguments read; appendices not inspected.

assumptions: The algorithm knows d,Delta,L1,L2,epsilon; queries any measurable points of R^d using the complete transcript and private randomness; computation between calls is unrestricted.
Each oracle call returns the exact pair (f(x),gradient f(x)); Hessian regularity does not grant Hessian or higher-derivative queries.
The output can be an unqueried point. The success requirement is separate for each fixed function, with probability over the algorithm's private randomness.
statement.conclusion: Q_rand,FO^infinity(epsilon;Delta,L1,L2)>=c Delta sqrt(L1) L2^(1/4) epsilon^(-7/4). The paper combines this new lower bound with the existing deterministic Li–Lin restarted accelerated-gradient upper bound to obtain Theta of the same expression in this regime; that upper bound is attributed, not newly established by this lower-bound record.
statement.objects_and_definitions: For each integer d>=1, F_1:2^(d)(Delta,L1,L2)={f in C²(R^d): f(0)-inf_x f(x)<=Delta, Lip(gradient f)<=L1, Lip(Hessian f)<=L2}. Norms are Euclidean and induced operator norms. Q_rand,FO^(d) is the least almost-sure oracle-call cap of an algorithm returning x_hat with ||gradient f(x_hat)||<=epsilon with probability >=2/3 for every f in that class. Q_rand,FO^infinity=sup_{d>=1} Q_rand,FO^(d).
statement.parameter_domains: epsilon<=c L1²/L2 and Delta sqrt(L2) epsilon^(-3/2)>=C. Dimension may be sufficiently large and depend on the horizon/parameters; no fixed-small-dimension bound is asserted.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: There exist absolute numerical constants c,C>0 such that for every positive parameter tuple satisfying the regime, the stated supremum-over-finite-dimensions lower bound holds. The hard distribution and sufficiently large finite dimension are chosen independently of the deterministic policy and private seed. A single fixed function is evaluated against randomized algorithm seeds; this is not an adversary choosing the instance after observing the seed.

use_restrictions: Literature statement and precise source-linked proof map; no independent whole-proof reproof or formal verification.
No fixed-small-dimension, noisy-gradient, finite-sum or higher-order-oracle lower bound.
Matching deterministic upper bound belongs to Li–Lin; its original paper was not independently checked here.
Reference readiness is a Curator proposal; independent Reviewer acceptance and publication remain external workflow steps.

research_use.reason: Provides the selected literature lower bound with explicit finite-dimension and accuracy qualifications.

source_refs.locator: Section 3.1 and Theorem 3.1, p.4; Table 1 p.3; Sections 4–8 pp.5–16

summary: In the stated high-accuracy, sufficiently-large-gap regime, Q_rand,FO^infinity is at least c Delta L1^(1/2) L2^(1/4) epsilon^(-7/4), for unrestricted adaptive randomized exact value-gradient algorithms.
title: Randomized exact first-order lower bound under gradient and Hessian Lipschitz regularity
use_when: Compare dimension-uniform first-order query complexity for nonconvex gradient stationarity under global gradient and Hessian Lipschitz bounds.
